items.note: Quasi-experiment with pretest-posttest control groups (31 + 31 fourth graders, Turkey) in which ChatGPT feedback supported creative writing; outcomes are a Creative Writing Product Evaluation Scale and a self-efficacy scale; non-random design.
Quasi-experiment with 29 fourth graders using AI image visualization tools in creative writing; the only quantitative outcome is the Writing Disposition Scale (an attitude measure), plus interviews.

Thesis with two experiments comparing generative-AI and non-AI groups on brainstorming (originality, flexibility, fluency, elaboration) and on the Divergent Associations Task (originality, semantic distance); sample sizes and assignment not given in the abstract.

Randomizes 331 participants to generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized LLM assistants for a marketing campaign task and scores campaign quality and creativity; all arms use AI (AI-configuration comparison); OSF preregistration mentions a no-AI condition, so check the full text for one.

ICCE 2023 proceedings paper: 34 high-school students in a synectics-plus-ChatGPT experimental group versus 30 controls on creative writing ability; abstract does not say how ability was measured or how groups were formed.

Fashion design workshops and interviews with 10 students ideating with image-generating AI; experts rated AI-assisted ideas higher in originality and novelty than a control group; very small sample, below the 50-person threshold.

Design-thinking AI education program for 117 Korean middle-school students (57 used generative AI in the Empathize stage, 60 did not); outcome is change in creative problem-solving ability, likely a pre-post measure taken after the program (after_ai), and the instrument (test or self-report scale) is not stated.

33 graduate engineering students in randomly formed teams brainstormed product ideas, with ChatGPT added to select groups (assignment of groups to ChatGPT not described as random); ideas rated for creativity by students and analyzed with NLP for homogeneity (across_people); below 50 participants.

76 Hong Kong secondary students randomly assigned to a five-week GenAI-driven storytelling intervention or traditional writing instruction; rubric-based writing assessment includes a creativity dimension, measured pre and post (likely after_ai); abstract taken from the journal PDF first page.

Ten polytechnic students split into two groups, one working with ChatGPT, on the Alternative Uses Test (fluency, flexibility, originality) and a creative storytelling task; very small sample, below the 50-person threshold.
